This appeal challenges the order dated 24.04.2025 passed by the High Court of Judicature at Bombay, Bench at Aurangabad rejecting Anticipatory Bail Appln. No. 1473 of 2024.

entities.text: High Court of Judicature at Bombay, Bench at Aurangabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Apprehending arrest in connection with crime registered pursuant to First Information Report No.
501/2024 dated 08.08.2024 lodged with Police Station Gangakhed, District Parbhani, in respect of offences punishable under Sections 376(1), 377 and 354A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC),
the appellant preferred the application before the High Court seeking anticipatory bail in terms of Section 438 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (CrPC).

Said application having been rejected,
the instant appeal has been preferred.
By order dated 07.05.2025, while issuing notice, this Court granted interim protection in favour of the appellant.

He submitted that the complainant is a married lady who is an adult and the husband of the complainant has been videographing the presence of the complainant along with the appellant herein; the entire endeavour of the Dyanoba Mugaji Karhale @ Mauli Maharaj ... vs State Of Maharashtra on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24966867/
1 complainant and her husband is only to create a false evidence as against the appellant herein for oblique purposes; that this Court had already granted interim protection by order dated 07.05.2025 subject to cooperation by the appellant.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said interim order may be made absolute and the appellant will cooperate with the investigation which is still on.

Per contra, learned counsel for the second respondent-complainant contended that the appellant has a tendency of exploiting minor girls and young women on the premise that he is a spiritual leader/godman in the Ashram in Gangakhed; that the second respondent-complainant is one such victim and there are several other victims; the allegations against the appellant are serious; that any protection by way of anticipatory bail granted to the appellant herein would frustrate the entire investigation as well as the subsequent trial.
In the circumstances, no leniency may be shown to the appellant herein and the appeal may be simply dismissed.
Learned counsel for the first respondent-State also endorsed the submissions of learned counsel for the second respondent-complainant.
Considering the circumstances on record, in our view, the appellant is entitled to the relief claimed under Section 438 of the CrPC.

We, therefore, allow this appeal, set-aside the order passed by the High Court and direct that in the event of his arrest, the Arresting Officer shall release the appellant on bail subject to furnishing cash security in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) with two like sureties.
It is directed that the appellant shall extend complete cooperation in the investigation.
The appellant shall not misuse his liberty and shall not in any way influence the witnesses or tamper with the material on record.
Any breach or infraction of the aforesaid conditions may entail cancellation of anticipatory bail.
With the aforesaid directions, the criminal appeal is allowed.
